title: Story Horizon
html:
That day, everyone in the Seoul Dome was engulfed in dazzling rays of light.

[Someone has cleared the tenth main scenario.]

[Congratulations. You have passed the tenth scenario.]

Those lucky enough to evade the demonic people and hide in the corners of the Seoul Dome, and those barely keeping themselves alive as they roamed the first and second floors of [Dark Castle].

All the incarnations who had somehow managed to stay alive amid the threats of the scenarios received the same message that day.

[You have earned the ‘Liberator of the Seoul Dome’ achievement.]

Liberation.

At first, they did not understand the word, but their bodies grasped its meaning before their minds did.

Twitching limbs.

Dilated pupils and trembling lips.

[You can escape the Seoul Dome.]

Their long-held wish had finally become reality.

Whoooooosh!

Everyone on the first and second floors of [Dark Castle] was summoned outside the castle at exactly the same time. And they all witnessed the same sight.

Rrrrrumble!

The collapsing Dark Castle.

That terrible nightmare which had seized all of Seoul was collapsing from the sky, like a sandcastle crumbling away. The broken chunks soon turned to dust and scattered. As people watched, an inexplicable sorrow washed over them.

“It's over.”

Someone said those words.

“We can get out······ We can live now······.”

“Hell is over!”

Some sensed that their tragedy was coming to an end.

Rewards rained down from thin air. Joy filled their faces. Even if another tragedy lay ahead, now was the time to savor their newfound freedom. But not everyone shared that feeling.

“······What happened to Dokja ajusshi?”

Kim Dokja's companions who had escaped [Dark Castle]. Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye, Gong Pildu, Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung, Han Sooyoung······. All of them had gathered in one place. People who were alive because of Kim Dokja, or who owed him a debt.

“Does anyone—does anyone know? Please, say something! Master! What happened to Dokja ajusshi!”

Each of the companions followed their instincts in search of someone who could explain what had happened. But the one person who could answer them remained silent. With his lips pressed tightly together, Yoo Joonghyuk stared at the collapsing [Dark Castle].

The collapsing [Dark Castle], as though an entire history were disappearing.

Kim Dokja had been there.

And he had died there.

With lifeless eyes, Yoo Joonghyuk merely reaffirmed that fact, over and over.

Kim Dokja was dead.

How could such a thing happen?

Yoo Joonghyuk felt like a stranger to himself, unable to make that fact feel real.

“Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi! Please say something! Please!”

With a dazed expression, Yoo Joonghyuk looked at Lee Hyunsung, who had grabbed him and was shaking him.

Neither in the first round nor in the second······ had he ever seen that expression on Lee Hyunsung's face.

Yoo Joonghyuk could scarcely remember the expressions his companions wore when they lost someone truly precious.

Because he had always been the one wearing that expression.

Because he alone had survived to the end and despaired in the face of tragedy.

But this life was different.

Many people were still by his side.

And they were experiencing someone's death alongside him.

“Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi!”

“Master!”

Everyone was looking at him.

Faces hoping he would tell them it wasn't too late.

But there was only one answer Yoo Joonghyuk could give those faces.

“I don't know either.”

Crushing the last hope they had.

Tragically, that was the role left to Yoo Joonghyuk.

“What happened to Kim Dokja······ I don't know either.”

In truth, he could have told them more.

What ‘scenario expulsion’ meant. He could have shared what he knew.

Or he could have spoken of the faint hope that there might still be a possibility.

But Yoo Joonghyuk did not.

Because he knew that speaking of it would amount to nothing more than a lengthy way of telling his companions this:

‘Kim Dokja is dead, and there is nothing you can do for him.’

Some words resonate all the more deeply because they go unspoken.

Some accepted Yoo Joonghyuk's silence, and some rejected Yoo Joonghyuk's silence. And all of them, in the end, understood that silence.

“Dokja hyung said it himself! He said he wouldn't die! He said he'd come back to life! Then why······!”

“Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi! Please tell us how to save Dokja-ssi!”

Despite Lee Gilyoung's and Lee Hyunsung's cries, Yoo Joonghyuk merely shakes his head.

If there were a way to save Kim Dokja, he would already have done it.

But he could not.

Perhaps it was not just him. Perhaps no one could.

[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ is overwhelmed by a profound sense of emptiness.]

[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ lies down on the spot.]

[The constellation ‘Seo Ae Il Pil’ breaks their pen.]

[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ stares into the abyss in bewilderment.]

.

.

[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula mourn the death of a constellation.]

[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula remember someone's name.]

Yoo Joonghyuk had never seen so many constellations speak of one person. Those lofty, arrogant constellations expressing emotions other than ‘frustration’ or ‘pleasure.’

As though they, too, had known such feelings.

The night sky shone, suffused with colors more brilliant than in any round of his life.

Sadness, grief, despair, sorrow······.

The night sky, composed of countless modifiers, shone forlornly.

Perhaps Kim Dokja had been a hope for them, too.

A hope that could show them a story different from all those before.

Something that could bring a change to this <Star Stream>.

‘It's not as though there's no way at all.’

Watching the dazzling stars' requiem rite (鎭魂祭), the regressor Yoo Joonghyuk thought.

‘If I were to regress again, even now······.’

An ability bound to his life, like a nuclear missile launch button he could press at any moment. Yoo Joonghyuk could use this ability to regress through death whenever he wished, and make better choices with the new information he had acquired in the future.

If he regressed now, Kim Dokja might come back to life.

But······.

―Yoo Joonghyuk, get a grip. I'm telling you not to fool yourself into thinking things will get better if you repeat them a few times.

What if he regressed again, and Kim Dokja wasn't there?

Or what if the Kim Dokja he met again did not act as he had this time?

For the first time, Yoo Joonghyuk grew afraid of something.

The Kim Dokja of this life was only the Kim Dokja of this life.

Even Shin Yoosung from the forty-first round had never spoken of Kim Dokja, and he had never met Kim Dokja in his previous rounds.

Even if he returned to the past, the Kim Dokja of this life would not return.

―So live ‘this round’ properly.

Choices he had always been able to make at least twice had now become irreversible.

He had met Kim Dokja in his third life, and they had become companions.

And he had lost Kim Dokja.

―Because this round you're trying to abandon might be the ‘one and only round’ in which you can see the end of this world as a ‘human.’

Yoo Joonghyuk bit down hard on his lip and rose to his feet.

As always, only words remain.

Just as everything in the <Star Stream> was a story, Yoo Joonghyuk now had to admit that Kim Dokja's words had firmly become a part of him.

[Come now, why aren't you moving? Surely you've received the system messages?]

A dokkaebi dispatched by the Bureau was looking down at the companions from midair.

[Aha, I see. You're all mourning ‘his’ death.]

The mockery in that tone enraged the companions. But not all of them reacted that way. Barely keeping her composure, Jung Heewon asked.

“······What happened to Dokja-ssi?”

[He was expelled from the scenarios.]

“I'm asking what that means. Is he alive or dead?”

[I don't know either. However, whether an incarnation or a constellation, a ‘being expelled from the scenarios’ cannot survive. That is all I know.]

Not even a constellation could survive. At those words, the companions' faces froze into expressions even colder than before. Lee Jihye snapped.

“But there has to be a way, right? A way to save him or something······!”

[There is nothing you can do as you are now. Frankly, I'm surprised you still harbor such feelings. Let me give you a word of advice. Stop entertaining useless thoughts and focus on the scenario in front of you. You haven't completely escaped the ‘Seoul Dome’ yet.]

Leaving them with those mocking words, the dokkaebi lightly snapped its fingers.

Messages poured out of thin air once again.

[An Escape Scenario is being assigned.]

[The Seoul Dome will close soon! Escape the Seoul Dome within half a day.]

[An escape route will be provided automatically.]

[If you do not escape the dome within the time limit, you will die.]

“Goddammit······.”

The companions looked at one another, but no answers were written on their faces. They had no choice anyway.

“······Let's get moving for now.”

They began to follow the designated route.

Running, swimming, and sometimes crossing railings, they kept racing toward the outskirts of Seoul. And when the route markers finally disappeared, they came face-to-face with a crowd.

“Those people······.”

All the incarnations remaining in the Seoul Dome had gathered there.

There seemed to be about a thousand of them.

Some familiar faces were among them.

The King of Beauty, Min Jiwon, and the Reclusive Loner, Han Donghoon, waving at them.

They were all people Kim Dokja had saved.

Those who recognized Yoo Joonghyuk and the companions greeted them with small bows.

“······So this is the place.”

The companions stopped and looked up together at the dome's inner wall. The enormous birdcage that had imprisoned them until now. At last, their chance to escape this prison had come. Everyone seemed excited, but no one readily stepped outside.

Like canaries that cannot readily fly out of a wide-open cage.

Instead, they looked around as though searching for something.

One by one, their gazes gathered.

Before long, all those eyes had settled on one person.

Han Sooyoung was the first to speak.

“Yoo Joonghyuk.”

Yoo Joonghyuk met Han Sooyoung's gaze.

She said nothing more, but Yoo Joonghyuk read something in her eyes.

‘Don't waste the chance Kim Dokja gave you.’

Yoo Joonghyuk blinked slowly, then stepped forward.

The vast crowd was waiting for him to speak.

For some declaration to commemorate this moment when liberation had finally come.

Looking at the crowd focused on him, Yoo Joonghyuk deliberated.

In his past lives, Yoo Joonghyuk had stood in such a position several times.

At times, he had been an eloquent speaker; at others, a charismatic leader.

Finding something to say to the crowd was not difficult.

But why?

This time, he did not want to say those things.

Instead, he said this.

“······I will not give up on this life.”

Thinking that probably no one here could understand his words.

Amid the terrible loneliness that came with that knowledge, Yoo Joonghyuk continued.

“So don't you give up either.”

He did not know whether anything had gotten through.

Yoo Joonghyuk turned away from the crowd and slowly walked toward the dome's inner wall.

And.

Boom!

Once.

Boooom!

Twice.

His fist, swung in fury, slammed into the wall.

Enormous cracks spread across the dome's inner wall from the point where his fist had struck.

Crrrack.

The wall they had never once been able to cross since the scenarios began. It crumbled little by little, until an exit large enough for one person to pass through opened.

A landscape that had always been there, yet remained beyond their reach.

Yoo Joonghyuk was the first to step into that landscape.

“Let's go.”

They stepped toward a scenario without Kim Dokja.

●

「And in the darkness, Kim Dokja, finally alone, awoke.」

“······Ugh.”

「His entire body ached as though every bone had been crushed, and his skin had stiffened like the hide of a dead animal.」

Listening to the voice of [Fourth Wall], I slowly opened my eyes. The voice of [Fourth Wall], which had been so irritating last time, could not have been more welcome.

「I'm alive. That was what Kim Dokja thought.」

Judging by the chatter of [Fourth Wall], my plan seemed to have succeeded.

Actually, there was no need to call it a success.

In a way, it had been only natural.

The [Fate] they had imposed on me was the death of ‘incarnation Kim Dokja.’

So naturally, Kim Dokja as a ‘constellation’ did not die.

If I were going to disappear that easily, I wouldn't have gone to all that trouble to build up Stories and become a constellation.

The question was what state I would be in, having revived as a ‘constellation’ without my incarnation body······.

“······Where am I?”

What I could see around me: ruined buildings and a half-destroyed eight-lane road.

Somehow, the scene was familiar.

“This place······?”

Not long after muttering those words, I realized what had become of me. I looked up. The night sky that had always been filled with the light of countless constellations. But there was nothing there.

The deep stillness that followed my muttering startled me as much as the fact that I had spoken to myself at all.

Looking at the night sky, I laughed hollowly.

“Haha······.”

Normally, countless indirect messages from the constellations should have appeared.

From the ‘Great Sage, Heaven's Equal,’ who enjoyed my muttering, or the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ who liked to give me a hard time······ or the ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire,’ who liked me for reasons I didn't quite understand. In any case, someone should have answered.

But no one answered my muttering.

No ‘Bald General of Justice’ polishing his head,

No ‘One-Eyed Maitreya’ throwing off his eyepatch whenever he was bored,

And no utterly shameless ‘Supreme Maegum.’

When the constellation messages I had been so sick of vanished, what remained, absurdly enough, was a terrible loneliness.

「Kim Dokja thought. I'm truly alone now.」

[You are currently expelled from the scenarios.]

I slowly looked around at the scenery again.

Beings who remain alive after being expelled from the scenarios are sent to the nearest ‘area outside scenario coverage.’

[You are currently in an area outside scenario coverage.]

And this ‘area outside coverage’ where I now stood was a place very familiar to me.

「Seoul.」

This was Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul.

Where the ‘War of Kings’ had taken place, and where I had destroyed the ‘Absolute Throne.’

But the fact that Seoul had become an area outside scenario coverage meant······.

My companions······ had escaped safely.

Feeling strangely overwhelmed, I looked toward where the ‘Seoul Dome’ had once stood. That place, once covered by a translucent membrane, was now enclosed by something like a thick barrier.

The scenarios of ‘Seoul’ were now completely over.

And my companions were moving on to a ‘scenario’ without me, making a new story. They were continuing to live there.

······Was that enough?

「Kim Dokja felt happy, yet somehow desolate.」

After thinking of my companions for a moment, I slowly turned.

「Now alone, Kim Dokja had something he needed to do. It was for this that he had chosen a gruesome death.」

●

「Throughout his walk through the streets of Seoul, Kim Dokja was immersed in memories that had not yet grown old. Everywhere he went, there were only places where he had undertaken scenarios with his companions. Once again, Kim Dokja realized anew that he had become part of ‘Ways of Survival.’ He had, unmistakably, lived this story.」

“······Sure, that's moving and all, but can't you stop now? How long are you going to keep muttering?”

「Kim Dokja snapped at the poor ‘Fourth Wall.’」

At first, I had liked the feeling of someone chattering beside me, but having it explain every little thing I did was far from pleasant.

「How much time has passed? Kim Dokja wanted to ask, but there was no one to answer him.」

“Goddammit. You could just answer me.”

After talking back to it, I decided to check my condition first.

[Many of your Stories are currently damaged.]

[Your incarnation body is currently in a state of complete collapse.]

I had survived through the Status of a constellation, but I had completely lost my incarnation body. In other words, I now existed not as a ‘physical body,’ but merely as an extremely incomplete mass of Stories.

Fssss.

[Your true body is currently in a highly precarious state.]

[No means of preserving your true body can be found.]

An unstable state in which I felt I might collapse completely at the slightest touch.

Living like this was hardly living at all.

For now, I decided to try everything I could.

[‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ cannot be used in this area.]

······So it wouldn't work after all?

[Communication with your incarnation is currently unavailable.]

This wouldn't work either.

I had expected it, but it felt strange when it actually didn't work.

It felt as though I had wandered alone into a place with no signal.

Of course, my actual situation was worse than that.

[You cannot use the channel system.]

Having been expelled from the scenarios, I had naturally been expelled from the channel as well, and my contract with Bihyung had naturally been terminated.

Looking at the sky without a single star, I felt an empty freedom come over me.

······Now I really was alone.

As I realized that, something like a chill began to seep into me.

「No one is watching me, and I, too, can see no one.」

No, perhaps I wasn't completely alone.

「In that stillness, Kim Dokja suddenly realizes. I see. Existence is something that can only be sensed through someone else's gaze.」

“I don't have philosophical thoughts like that, idiot. More to the point, how long are you going to keep this up?”

「The foolish Kim Dokja did not know. Why the great ‘Fourth Wall’ was going to all this trouble.」

······Oh, getting cheeky, are you?

“So you can do more than just explain things? What the hell are you? Are you really a skill?”

「The foolish Kim Dokja spoke to himself, addressing empty air.」

This little bastard, seriously.

「The foolish Kim Dokja······.」

“Will you stop? Want me to turn the skill off?”

At that moment, a crackling sound came from thin air.

「‘Fourth Wall’ says. ‘Th en sh all I st op?’」

I was a little surprised.

This thing could express its intentions much more clearly than I'd thought?

Come to think of it, last time, too······.

“Yeah, stop. I don't want to be disturbed right now.”

[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ falls silent.]

But the very next moment, I immediately regretted that choice.

Crrrrrack.

Before I could even say “What?”, I felt the air around me freeze.

The chill seeped straight into my skin and penetrated deep into my bones. With a faint crumbling sound, I felt the breath catch in my lungs.

“Ghk······?”

In that instant, certain things belatedly came to mind.

Why those bastards from <Vedas> and <Olympus> had gone out of their way to send me to an ‘area outside scenario coverage.’

It was because they had been aiming for precisely this situation.

Their scheme to dispose of ‘constellation Kim Dokja’ while killing ‘incarnation Kim Dokja.’

“Ghk, ghuuuugh······.”

I screamed, but no scream comes out.

I wanted to breathe, but I cannot breathe.

My breath caught, as though someone had crushed my lungs.

My mind turns blank, and my thoughts are erased one by one.

The <Star Stream> is a world of ‘stories.’

Incarnation or constellation, there are no exceptions.

All beings breathe through ‘stories’ and exist through ‘stories.’

[The rate of Story damage is increasing!]

[Your existence is beginning to disappear.]

So where no ‘stories’ exist, nothing can exist.

Not even me.

Fssss!

‘Goddammit, save me!’

I cried out amid the fathomless terror of my own disappearance.

Only then did I understand why [Fourth Wall] had been making such a racket.

It had kept chattering on about something to keep me alive.

To keep me alive in a place where no stories existed······.

It had kept telling me a ‘story.’

[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates!]

「‘Fourth Wall’ says. ‘Id i ot.’」

At last, my airway opened and I managed to breathe again.

“Hah, hah······.”

I had known that those expelled from the scenarios suffered a terrible fate, but I hadn't known it would be this bad.

Then again, even ‘Cheok Jungyeong’ could not survive exclusion from the scenarios without the help of a <nebula>······ Damn it, it seemed I'd underestimated the situation.

I'd thought that, at the cost of a few Stories, I would somehow be able to make it to my first destination······.

Without [Fourth Wall], even staying alive might have been difficult.

「Kim Dokja thought. I must never get cheeky with ‘Fourth Wall’-nim again.」

Even in my misery, I couldn't bring myself to argue with that.

“······But how long can you protect me?”

「‘Fourth Wall’ says. ‘Not for l ong.’」

Bzzzzzt!

No sooner had [Fourth Wall] spoken than fierce sparks erupted around me.

Then again, it was strange in itself that [Fourth Wall] could single-handedly bear a probability burden that would require intervention on the scale of a <nebula> to resolve.

I didn't have much time.

If I didn't finish what I needed to do in time, I would wither away and die here.

Ssssssss.

It was then that I heard a noise from somewhere.

A sucking sound reminiscent of a vacuum cleaner······.

「Kim Dokja knew what those things were.」

“Yeah, I know. Scenario Cleaners.”

The appearance of the Cleaners meant that a large-scale ‘cleanup’ of this scenario area had begun.

「Kim Dokja thought. Now that the cleanup has begun, a ‘Demon of the Horizon’ will appear before long. Those hyena-like creatures that roam the ruins of scenarios would never pass up ruins as delectable as these.」

It really was astonishingly good at reading my thoughts.

But before meeting them, there was something I needed to find first.

「Kim Dokja quickened his pace.」

Stumbling, I gradually increased my running speed.

Things resembling small dark clouds were drifting through the streets.

Those were the ‘Scenario Cleaners.’

They were creatures I needed to watch out for, but I ran on without paying them any mind.

The ‘Cleaners’ were slow, anyway, and their detection range was narrow.

As long as I carefully avoided them, reaching my destination without being detected wouldn't be difficult.

I immediately left Gwanghwamun and began heading south.

Through Euljiro 3-ga, Chungmuro, Dongguk University, Yaksu, Geumho Station······.

Like a salmon, I retraced the places I had passed through until now.

And Oksu Station, which I finally reached.

There, I came upon the broken Dongho Bridge.

As I looked at the broken bridge, memories still vivid flashed through my mind.

This was where that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk had thrown me into the ichthyosaur's mouth.

I wondered if he was doing all right now.

Well, Han Sooyoung was there, too, so they were probably helping each other and doing fine.

······All I could do was hope so.

Whoosh!

Without even a running start, I easily leaped across the broken bridge. Once, I had barely managed to cross it with the help of ‘Deus Ex Machina,’ but now a single leap was enough.

It was a moment that showed how much had changed since the scenarios began.

But I still had a long way to go.

Because the ones I had to overcome awaited me across a distance far more daunting than the gap in that broken bridge.

Tap.

At the place I finally reached stood a half-destroyed subway train.

The place where all these scenarios had begun.

After looking at the train's exterior for a moment, I went inside and began searching the wreckage.

How long had I been at it?

At last, I found what I was looking for.

It was an item box glowing white.

A short scenario message had been left on the item box.

―Kim Dokja, I can trust you, right? For now, I'm leaving this as you requested and heading out. Thank you for being an incarnation in my channel all this time.

It was a message whose author was very easy to identify.

―Please, be alive.

Of course. I don't die.

I opened the item box.

Inside the box were the attribute I had paid a whopping 300,000 coins to purchase, and all the items I had requested.

[You have acquired a new attribute.]

[You have acquired the item ‘Dokkaebi Egg.’]

[You have acquired the item ‘Unbreakable Faith.’]

······.

After collecting all the items, I stepped out of the train.

Dawn was breaking just then.

Sitting on the edge of the bridge, I waited.

It would be here soon.

And no sooner had I thought that than someone appeared on the horizon where the story had ended.

A stooped old man with an enormous lump on one cheek.

He was walking toward me with a peculiar expression.

As though he had known I was here.

“Are you the ‘Demon King of Salvation’?”

After looking at him for a moment, I turned my gaze toward the light of dawn beyond the dome.

And I thought of the nebulas that would be waiting for me beyond that light.

They probably thought I was dead by now.

<Olympus>. <Vedas>. <Papyrus>······.

I recalled their modifiers, one by one.

All those constellations who mocked the incarnations' stories, treated them with contempt, and finally made them into their own entertainment.

Just wait a little longer.

「I'll bring every last one of you down from that goddamned sky.」

There is a passage like this in ‘Ways of Survival.’

「Demons live on the ‘Story Horizon.’ Beings called ‘demons,’ though they are neither Demon Kings nor members of a demon species. Beings who crave stories as much as the dokkaebis do, and hate the dokkaebis as much as they crave stories.」

······Yes, that passage.

「If you have been expelled from the scenarios, there is only one thing you can hope for. The mercy of the ‘Demons of the Horizon.’」

Since [Fourth Wall] was doing all the talking on its own, there was nothing left for me to say.

I looked at the ‘Demon of the Horizon.’

An elderly appearance. At a glance, his attire resembled a vagabond's, but recognizing him was not difficult. Because every ‘Demon of the Horizon’ has an enormous lump on their cheek. For that reason, some also call them ‘Wenny men’ for short.

Bzzzzt!

Faint sparks flickered in midair, and the Wenny man took a step back.

“······How unusual. I cannot check your information even with ‘Great Demon's Eyes’?”

Apparently, he had already been trying hard to pry into my information. Yellow light swirled in one of the Wenny man's eyes.

[Great Demon's Eyes].

The Wenny man had those same eyes that Anna Croft had possessed.

It was probably only natural.

He was probably the one who had told Anna about ‘Great Demon's Eyes,’ after all.

Demons of the Horizon were incomparably more dangerous than an idiot like Bihyung. If he underestimated me even a little, I would be the one devoured.

Deliberately acting at ease, I opened the conversation.

“Not even the Prophet can read my information. A Wenny man with outdated information? That's unlike you.”

The Wenny man frowned, as though his pride had been wounded.

“······Did you know I would come?”

“Yes.”

“How?”

“You probably came for this.”

I took out the dokkaebi egg I had tucked against my chest and showed it to him.

The Wenny man's gaze wavered.

He, too, had recognized the being inside this egg.

“That soul is mine.”

At the same time, the demon's lump began to swell ominously.

“My counterpart in another parallel dimension sent that soul here. Ownership of that soul belongs to me.”

He took a step toward me, so I took a step back and feigned ignorance.

“I don't know what you're talking about.”

“······I wondered where the soul that should have returned from the Underworld had gone. So you intercepted it. It is not too late yet. I ask that you return the soul.”

“Return it? What nonsense is that? Does the <Star Stream> have a lost property law or something?”

Still at the same distance, the Wenny man stared at the egg with eyes steeped in greed.

I looked down at the egg as well.

Inside this egg was Shin Yoosung from Yoo Joonghyuk's ‘forty-first round.’

So in a sense, the ‘Demon of the Horizon’ was right.

The one who had transformed Shin Yoosung into a ‘disaster’ and sent her to this dimension was the Wenny man before my eyes.

The furrow between the Wenny man's brows deepened.

“If you wish to play word games······.”

“Let's ask her directly. She has free will, too.”

Without delay, I tapped the egg's surface and asked.

“Yoosung, he says he's your owner. What do you think?”

The egg, quivering violently.

“Hmm, I see. You're saying he's not?”

“······Listen.”

Ignoring the Wenny man, I spoke to the egg again.

“Then who do you belong to?”

This time, the egg shook with a shudder.

I nodded as though I understood.

“Yes, that's right. A ‘soul’ can't belong to anyone. Just as no one can own a ‘story.’”

No one can own a ‘story.’

At those words, a sharp look flitted across the Wenny man's face.

[Great Demon's Eyes] spun around.

A smile settled on his lips, as though he found this interesting.

“Interesting, Demon King of Salvation. Are you proposing to negotiate with me?”

Got you.

I grinned and answered.

“That's right.”

“······Very well. Your exploits have been followed with considerable interest on this side, too. But if you wish to negotiate, hand over that egg first.”

“Don't you know what negotiation means? That won't work. I need this one.”

“You do not know that egg's value.”

“No, I do.”

The egg clung tightly to my hand, as though unwilling to leave me.

Gently stroking the egg, I continued.

“Because the beings born from this egg can create ‘channels.’”

“······Do you know what that means?”

“It means they can transmit Star Stream broadcasts beyond the Bureau's authority.”

At my words, the Wenny man's lump trembled faintly.

Flustered, he moved his fingertips toward his beard.

I added.

“In other words, this egg has the power to create countless ‘stories.’ That's why you want it, isn't it?”

Seemingly quite taken aback, the Wenny man was silent for a moment.

Jung Heewon could hardly believe she was enjoying such a luxury after so long. Everything was peaceful. She didn't have to stay awake all night for fear of a monster attack, or be wary of other humans for fear they'd steal her items.
